key_insight: A 2D DNS/DLM-FD model reproduces the main gap-dependent spin-coupling regimes of a two-rotor corral, but shifts the Reynolds-number spin-reversal boundary and changes the underlying torque mechanism.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict when a passive rotor will corotate or counterrotate in confined viscous flows, which is useful for microfluidic mixers, rotor arrays, and hydrodynamic coupling design.
method: Direct numerical simulation of 2D incompressible viscous flow.
DLM/FD formulation for active-passive rotor dynamics and torque balance.
Phase-diagram sweeps over gap G and Reynolds number Re for corral sizes C = 3, 4.5, and 6.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark agreement at Re = 20, including counterrotation, wide-gap corotation, and vortex attachment/detachment/merger sequences, plus a Re-driven boundary shift at higher Re.
watch_item: The model is strictly planar, so missing finite-depth effects and end-wall stresses may explain why the experimental spin-reversal mechanism and boundary location are not fully matched.
paper_title: Two-dimensional simulations of hydrodynamic spin coupling in a two-rotor corral
